$comment: c111 (D-RUNTIME-PE-MAIN-ARGS): the WIDE program-entry RUN witness (the wmain(int,wchar_t**) counterpart of the narrow main_argc_argv). On the pe64 target the Windows OS entry receives NO C argument vector, so the MIR-tier synthesized pre-main init (realizeEntryShape in src/mir/merge/synth_pe_startup.cpp) calls the UCRT WIDE populate export _configure_wide_argv(1) and dereferences __p___wargv (plus the SHARED __p___argc -- MEASURED: argc is common to the narrow and wide worlds, so one accessor serves both) to populate argc/argv, then forwards them to wmain. The WIDE arm is chosen by the RESOLVED ENTRY'S SIGNATURE, never a format flag: the entry matches the LANGUAGE's `wmain` row fn(i32, ptr-ptr-u16) -> i32, whose materialization verb is `argc-wargv`, and pe64-x86_64-windows-exec is the only shipped format that declares `argc-wargv` in its `entryVerbs` -- which is ALSO why this example is pe64-only rather than merely untested elsewhere: on ELF and Mach-O `wmain` does not survive candidate selection at all, so a `wmain`-only source there has NO program entry (K_ProgramEntryUndefined, pinned by entry_wmain_only_refused_elf). UCRT-P4 replaced c111's msvcrt __wgetmainargs here, because __getmainargs/__wgetmainargs are msvcrt-ONLY exports (MEASURED 2026-08-10, objdump -p: msvcrt ord 138 / 167, ucrtbase exports NEITHER) and could not survive the CRT migration. The runner spawns with no extra args -> wmain must see argc==1 + a non-empty WIDE argv[0] (argv[0][0] is its first u16 code unit) + argv[1]==NULL -> exit 42; each failed layer exits a distinct 90..94 (see main.c). pe64-ONLY: wmain+wide-argv is a Windows construct; the ELF stack-vector mechanism hands a NARROW char** vector, a category mismatch for a wide entry, so no ELF target is declared. * UCRT-P4 REMOVED A MACH-O TARGET THAT THIS SENTENCE ALREADY SAID SHOULD NOT EXIST. The manifest declared `arm64:macho64-arm64-darwin-exec` alongside the pe64 one, contradicting its own pe64-ONLY claim, and the entry-shape gate is what surfaced it: macho declares no `ptr-ptr-u16` entry shape, so the wide entry is now REFUSED there. WHY THE PREVIOUS ACCEPTANCE WAS WRONG (INFERRED from the mechanism, not measured -- no Mac was available): the macho exec formats declare NO `processArgs`, because dyld hands LC_MAIN its arguments in the argument registers, so the pre-UCRT-P4 synth was a no-op there and the trampoline passed dyld's NARROW `char**` straight into a parameter typed `unsigned short**`. The four runtime checks below survive that misread by accident -- argv[0] is non-null and argv[0][0] reads the first TWO ASCII bytes as one non-zero u16 -- so the arm reported success while reading a narrow vector as wide. The fix is REMOVAL, not declaring the shape on macho: declaring it would assert a realization that has no materialization arm and no run witness, which is the accepted-then-wrong outcome the gate exists to prevent. A genuine Darwin wide-entry witness needs its own cycle (D-RUNTIME-MAIN-ENVP-ENTRY-SHAPE covers the Darwin entry-shape family, including its FOUR-parameter form). RED-on-disable: remove `processArgs` from the pe64 shipped exec JSON (runtime-read config) -> the synth never runs -> wmain reads garbage entry-register argc -> exit 90 instead of 42.
